centralPlot: When a storm injures her mentor, apprentice lantern keeper Mara must choose between a magistrate's threat to her future and her duty to light the harbour lantern before an approaching ship reaches a dangerous reef.

characters.name: Mara
explicitMotivations: Protect sailors who depend on the harbour lantern
Earn Ivo's trust and qualify as a licensed lantern keeper
flawsOrAmbiguities: She is frightened by the credible threat to the future she has worked toward

characters.name: Ivo
explicitMotivations: Keep the harbour lantern operating safely
Teach Mara to understand the responsibility of the work

characters.name: Magistrate Rusk
explicitMotivations: Delay a rival's ship so his own business gains the first berth
flawsOrAmbiguities: Uses official power over apprenticeship papers for private commercial advantage

relationships.powerDynamics: Ivo has teaching authority but treats Mara's responsibility seriously and supports her judgment.

relationships.nature: Apprentice confronted by an official who wants her cooperation
relationships.powerDynamics: Rusk can influence Mara's qualification papers and uses that power to threaten her future.

coreStoryBeats.summary: A storm injures Ivo, leaving Mara responsible for an unlit harbour lantern before the Gull Star arrives.
Rusk asks Mara to leave the lantern dark so a rival ship misses the tide.
Rusk threatens Mara's apprenticeship when she refuses.
Mara chooses her duty to sailors despite the threat and climbs the tower with the spare oil.
Mara lights the lantern before the Gull Star reaches Black Tooth Reef, allowing the captain to correct course and pass safely.
Mara reports Rusk's threat; his authority over apprenticeship papers is removed during an investigation, while Mara remains Ivo's apprentice.

developmentBeats.summary: Mara has spent two years learning the practical work of maintaining the lantern.
Mara explicitly fears losing the future she has planned but remembers why sailors depend on the light.

enrichmentMaterial.summary: Greyhaven's harbour and Black Tooth Reef establish the physical setting and danger.
The final exchange of the oil can shows Ivo's increased trust without turning Mara's choice into a reward ceremony.

causalDependencies.cause: Ivo is injured and cannot climb the tower.
causalDependencies.effect: Mara must prepare and light the lantern herself.
causalDependencies.whyItMatters: The injury creates the circumstance in which Mara must act independently.

causalDependencies.cause: The lantern is dark during a storm and Black Tooth Reef is difficult to see.
causalDependencies.effect: The approaching Gull Star needs the lantern to correct its course safely.
causalDependencies.whyItMatters: This establishes the concrete stakes behind Mara's decision.

causalDependencies.cause: Rusk controls apprenticeship paperwork and threatens Mara with losing her future.
causalDependencies.effect: Mara faces a meaningful personal cost for refusing his demand.
causalDependencies.whyItMatters: The coercive power relationship makes her choice difficult rather than effortless.

causalDependencies.cause: Mara lights the lantern before the Gull Star reaches the reef.
causalDependencies.effect: The captain sees the light, corrects course, and passes Black Tooth Reef safely.
causalDependencies.whyItMatters: The climax depends on the timing and causal effect of Mara's action.

iconicMaterial.textOrDescription: The harbour lantern shining through the storm as the Gull Star approaches Black Tooth Reef
iconicMaterial.importance: This is the central visual expression of Mara choosing duty over Rusk's threat.

iconicMaterial.textOrDescription: Rusk's demand does not change what the lantern is for.
iconicMaterial.importance: This captures Mara's reasoning without adding a moral lesson from outside the story.

intenseMaterial.description: Ivo badly twists his ankle and cannot climb the tower.
intenseMaterial.narrativeFunction: Forces Mara to take responsibility for lighting the lantern.

intenseMaterial.description: A ship approaches a difficult-to-see reef during a storm while the harbour lantern is dark.
intenseMaterial.narrativeFunction: Creates immediate stakes for Mara's decision.

adaptationRisks.description: Mara's choice can be flattened into wanting praise or a reward.
adaptationRisks.whatMustBePreserved: Her established motives are protecting sailors, accepting responsibility, and earning trust through the work itself.

adaptationRisks.description: The rescue can stop depending on Mara lighting the lantern before the Gull Star reaches the reef.
adaptationRisks.whatMustBePreserved: Mara's timely action must cause the captain to see the danger and correct course.

adaptationRisks.description: Rusk's threat can be softened into friendly advice or ordinary disagreement.
adaptationRisks.whatMustBePreserved: Rusk uses real institutional power over Mara's apprenticeship to pressure her for private gain.

adaptationRisks.description: The adaptation can retain names while losing the lighthouse duty, coercive choice, and reef rescue.
adaptationRisks.whatMustBePreserved: The story remains about Mara choosing to light the harbour lantern despite Rusk's threat, thereby protecting the Gull Star.
